title: Approvals status mirror drops the acting user, forcing every downstream record-change flow to `runAs:'system'`
body:
Found while surveying #3760's blast radius.

`approval-service.ts:977` writes the decision back onto the target business record with a bare system context:

```ts
await this.engine.update(object, { id: recordId, [field]: status }, { context: SYSTEM_CTX });
```

where `SYSTEM_CTX` (`:144`) is `{ isSystem: true, positions: [], permissions: [] }` — **no `userId`**. Six call sites stamp a status this way: `:1230` (pending), `:1432` (approved/rejected), `:1539` (recalled), `:1639` (revision budget exhausted), `:1677` (returned), `:2335` (dead-run sweep).

Every one of those is an action **a specific human just took** — a submitter submitting, an approver approving. The identity is known at the call site and thrown away.

Consequence, now that #3760 refuses user-less data ops: any record-change flow bound to that object — "when the invoice is approved, do X", the single most natural approvals automation — has no trigger user, so it must declare `runAs: 'system'` or be refused. Authors are pushed to blanket elevation for a case where a perfectly good scoped identity existed.

**The fix already has a first-party precedent in the same plugin.** `approval-node.ts:152-157` re-attaches the acting user onto the system context:

```ts
{ ...SYSTEM_CTX, userId: context?.userId }
```

Doing the same on the status mirror would let those cascades run as the deciding user with RLS enforced, instead of requiring elevation. Worth checking the other `SYSTEM_CTX` writers in that file against the same standard.

Note the mirror write must stay `isSystem` (the submitter generally cannot edit a locked/submitted record) — this is about adding attribution to it, not removing elevation.

Refs #3760, #3703.
